champion: Calcific Tendinitis of the Longus Colli Muscle
ordered_diagnoses: Calcific Tendinitis of the Longus Colli Muscle

s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of posterior neck pain with limited cervical range of motion and odynophagia
salient_findings: Severe reduction in active cervical range of motion due to pain
Retropharyngeal thickening at the upper cervical spine
Soft-tissue calcification anterior to the C1 arch
key_facts: No history of upper respiratory infection
Retropharyngeal thickening on lateral cervical-spine radiograph
Soft-tissue calcification on unenhanced CT of the cervical spine

shortlist: Calcific Tendinitis of the Longus Colli Muscle

shortlist.label: Calcific Tendinitis of the Longus Colli Muscle
shortlist.why_kept: Matches case facts of acute onset posterior neck pain, limited cervical range of motion, and radiographic evidence of soft-tissue calcification

shortlist.label: Retropharyngeal Abscess
shortlist.why_kept: Consistent with severe neck pain, odynophagia, and radiographic retropharyngeal thickening, although fever is mild

shortlist.label: Tuberculous Cervical Spondylitis
shortlist.why_kept: Could explain chronic inflammation and calcification, but less likely given acute presentation and lack of systemic symptoms

shortlist.label: Cervical Spine Osteomyelitis
shortlist.why_kept: Possible cause of neck pain and elevated inflammatory markers, but less specific radiographic findings

shortlist.label: Infectious Spondylodiscitis
shortlist.why_kept: Considered due to presence of inflammation and potential for infection, but would expect more pronounced systemic symptoms

s4.champion: Calcific Tendinitis of the Longus Colli Muscle

raw.champion: Calcific Tendinitis of the Longus Colli Muscle
raw.rationale: The presence of soft-tissue calcification on CT and retropharyngeal thickening, combined with the acute onset of posterior neck pain, sore throat, and odynophagia without a history of trauma or infection, points towards Calcific Tendinitis of the Longus Colli Muscle as the most likely diagnosis.

rejected.label: Retropharyngeal Abscess
rejected.why: The lack of significant fever, normal oropharyngeal examination, and absence of neurologic deficits make this less likely.

rejected.label: Tuberculous Cervical Spondylitis
rejected.why: The acute presentation and lack of systemic symptoms such as weight loss or night sweats, along with the specific imaging findings, make this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Cervical Spine Osteomyelitis
rejected.why: The absence of significant fever, normal laboratory tests for infection, and the specific location of calcification and thickening do not support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Infectious Spondylodiscitis
rejected.why: The clinical presentation and imaging findings do not specifically indicate disc space infection or significant vertebral body involvement, making this diagnosis less likely.
